chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
The vessels of gold and silver are belongings of those who have no conviction.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of using gold and silver vessels in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) identifies gold and silver vessels as the exclusive domain of those lacking firm conviction (yaqin), a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence which often distinguishes between the practical prohibition (karahah or haram) of using these materials for daily consumption and the spiritual warning against ostentatious wealth. This narration, found in al-Kafi, underscores the theological link between material attachment and spiritual uncertainty, suggesting that the luxury of precious metal tableware reflects an inner lack of certainty in the Hereafter. The ruling is frequently discussed by scholars like al-Majlisi in Bihr al-Anwar, who contextualizes it within broader discussions on adornment and the transient nature of worldly status.
